sents.t: In the spring, Mr. Lee had offered to sponsor me for a green card, so I could live and work in America permanently.
After months of paperwork, I finally got a letter: my interview was on October 28th.
The night before, I couldn’t sleep.
Rosa told me that I should bring every document twice.
Lily made me practice my answers in the kitchen.
At the immigration office, I waited for an hour.
Then an officer called my name.
She asked me to raise my right hand and promise to tell the truth.
She asked me where I worked and how long I had worked there.
She asked me who my manager was and what my salary was.
Then she asked me why I wanted to stay in the United States.
Then I told her that I had come here for a job, but that I had found a home.
I said that my neighbors had become my family.
She looked up from her papers and smiled for the first time.
She said that she had heard many answers to that question, but that mine was one of the nicest.
Three weeks later, a small card arrived in the mail.
It was the most beautiful card I’d ever seen.

o: live and work in America permanently

comp.q: What was Sam’s answer to the last question?
o: He came for a job but found a home.
comp.fa: پاسخ سام به سؤال آخر چه بود؟

comp.q: How did the officer react to Sam’s answer?
o: She smiled and said it was one of the nicest answers.
She asked him to come back.
comp.fa: مأمور چه واکنشی به پاسخ سام نشان داد؟
